newsitem.title: USA: Olin reaches settlement with government.
newsitem.headline: Olin reaches settlement with government.

text.p: Olin Corp. said Thursday it had agreed to pay $8 million to the Department of Justice to settle allegations of discrepancies in the inspection of 20 mm ammunition produced at one of the company's facilities.
Olin, with businesses in defence and aerospace, did not admit liability in the settlement with the U.S. Attorney General's Office for the Southern District of Illinois.

The Norwalk, Conn.-based company said the settlement would allow it to complete a feasibility study into spinning off its Ordnance and Aerospace divisions to its shareholders, which was announced in November.
It said the settlement followed an investigation by the Attorney General's Office into the "in-process" inspection of ammunition at its Ordnance Division facility in Marion, Ill.
The company said the investigation began after it notified the Department of Defence that one of its employees had disclosed discrepancies in the inspection of the rounds, namely 28/B and M940.

It said the discrepancies did not adversely affect the rounds made for the U.S. Armed Forces and production had resumed. Olin's stock rose $1.50 to $80.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
